methods.label: Eliminate the common first term
methods.explanation:
All terms are positive, so \(a>0\) and \(r_1,r_2>0\). Each series has a finite sum. A ratio at least \(1\) would make every term at least \(a\), so both ratios must satisfy \(0<r_j<1\).

The infinite geometric-series formula therefore applies:
\[
\frac{a}{1-r_1}=r_1,
\qquad
\frac{a}{1-r_2}=r_2.
\]
Since the denominators are positive, these equations give
\[
a=r_1-r_1^2=r_2-r_2^2.
\]
Subtracting eliminates the unknown common first term:
\[
\begin{aligned}
0&=(r_1-r_2)-(r_1^2-r_2^2)\\
&=(r_1-r_2)(1-r_1-r_2).
\end{aligned}
\]
The series have the same positive first term and are different, so their ratios are different. Thus \(r_1-r_2\ne0\), forcing
\[
r_1+r_2=\boxed{1},
\]
choice C.
